Samir Kaur (Support): Allison from the auditor team just asked for SOC 2 evidence around data retention and access logs tied to the Feb billing incident. They want representative sample object IDs, KMS access events, and repro steps to show how we correlated the billing spike.
Megan Li (Eng-Security): Ack. Can you paste the auditor's exact asks? we should split: retention policy evidence, access logs for KMS/HSM ops, and the repro timeline for the billing anomaly.
Allison Morales (Auditor): Thanks Samir — we need: 1) a list of 10 sample customer object IDs showing retention lifecycle metadata (created, last-accessed, deleted/retention expiration). 2) KMS key-access audit events for those objects during the period 2026-02-10 to 2026-02-18. 3) the repro steps + queries you used to link the spike to a retry storm from service X. Prefer CSV and a hashed list (SHA256) for object IDs. Please also include the exact queries/commands you ran.
Samir Kaur (Support): copying the ticket here: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-4521 — we'll attach evidence there. I'm going to pull sample IDs and ask infra to export KMS logs.
Kevin Ortiz (Eng-Infra): I can run the export but need the sample IDs and confirmation of which KMS key ARN(s) to include. Also note: HSM hosted key material does not include private key data in logs; we only have request metadata.
Priya Nair (Compliance): For retention policy evidence: our canonical policy is 90 days for API logs, 7 years for billing receipts. Make sure you label which dataset corresponds to which policy. Auditor will want the policy doc link too.

Kevin Ortiz (Eng-Infra): Yep. I'll run an Athena query against our access logs. Query I plan to run: 
```
SELECT timestamp, principal_id, operation, resource_id, request_id
FROM kms_access_logs
WHERE resource_id IN ('obj-cust-00452-20260211','obj-cust-00110-20260212', 'obj-cust-00987-20260212', 'obj-cust-00221-20260213', 'obj-cust-00533-20260213', 'obj-cust-00770-20260214', 'obj-cust-00005-20260214', 'obj-cust-00644-20260215', 'obj-cust-00331-20260216', 'obj-cust-00888-20260217')
AND timestamp BETWEEN TIMESTAMP '2026-02-10 00:00:00' AND TIMESTAMP '2026-02-18 23:59:59'
ORDER BY timestamp;
```
Kevin Ortiz (Eng-Infra): ETA for export: 3 hours after I get the final list and the key ARNs. I'll queue the job. evidence-bot: note — long exports may be throttled, will chunk by day.
Allison Morales (Auditor): Chunked exports are fine, but we need a clear mapping of which chunk covers which timestamps. Also prefer SHA256 hashed IDs in a separate file so we don't get raw PII in transit.
Megan Li (Eng-Security): On the billing repro: I reproduced our local analysis that shows a retry loop from service-x (internal id svc-x-queue) that produced a burst of 502s which retried and caused duplicate charge attempts in the billing pipeline between 2026-02-12T03:20 and 2026-02-12T04:10 UTC. I'll paste the repro steps and the exact queries I used to correlate errors -> billing events.
Megan Li (Eng-Security): Repro steps (short):
1) Run the request log query to extract 502 errors by request_id during the window.
2) Cross-join request_id to billing_events where attempt_count > 1.
3) Identify duplicated invoice records with matching request_id.
Queries used: 
```
-- step 1
SELECT request_id, ts, status_code, backend
FROM request_logs
WHERE status_code = 502 AND ts BETWEEN '2026-02-12T03:00:00Z' AND '2026-02-12T05:00:00Z';
-- step 2
SELECT r.request_id, b.invoice_id, b.amount, b.attempts
FROM (
  SELECT request_id FROM request_logs WHERE status_code = 502 AND ts BETWEEN '2026-02-12T03:20:00Z' AND '2026-02-12T04:10:00Z'
) r
JOIN billing_events b ON b.request_id = r.request_id
WHERE b.attempts > 1;
```
Megan Li (Eng-Security): I can produce a small CSV with the correlated rows by EOD.
Samir Kaur (Support): great. Priya — can you confirm the policy doc link and that 90-day retention for API logs is sufficient for this request? Auditor asked whether we ever purge earlier than 90 days.
Priya Nair (Compliance): Policy link: https://redwood-internal/docs/compliance/data-retention-v2.0.md — we do not purge API access logs earlier than 90 days; older aggregated metrics exist longer but raw logs are 90d. For billing receipts, ledger entries are retained 7 years. I'll attach a signed policy snapshot for the auditor.
